rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken Cantonese phrase for movement towards the west.

example.english: Walk west from here for five minutes and you’ll reach the MTR station.
example.traditional: 由呢度向西行五分鐘就到地鐵站喇。
example.jyutping: jau4 ni1 dou6 hoeng3 sai1 haang4 ng5 fan1 zung1 zau6 dou3 dei6 tit3 zaam6 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something westward or western.

example.english: We will arrive if we walk west.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hoeng3 sai1 haang4 zau6 dou3 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the compass direction west.

example.english: The sun sets in the west.

rows.note: Use this for the western side or area of a place in everyday speech.

example.english: There’s a convenience store west of my home.
example.traditional: 我屋企西邊有間便利店。
example.jyutping: ngo5 uk1 kei2 sai1 bin1 jau5 gaan1 bin6 lei6 dim3

rows.note: Use this for a defined western region or western part, especially in geographic or written contexts.

example.english: This railway leads to the west of China.
example.traditional: 呢條鐵路通往中國西部。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 tit3 lou6 tung1 wong5 zung1 gwok3 sai1 bou6

rows.note: Use this specifically for inhabitants or people from a western region.

example.english: People from the west all wear thick coats in winter.
example.jyutping: sai1 bou6 jan4 dung1 tin1 dou1 zoek3 hau5 lau1

rows.jyutping: jau4 sai1 min6 ceoi1 lei4 ge3 N
rows.note: Use this attributive construction specifically for wind coming from the west.

example.english: The wind coming from the west is really strong.
example.jyutping: jau4 sai1 min6 ceoi1 lei4 ge3 fung1 hou2 daai6
